diagnosis: The scenario fails because C1 (remote instruction day) is a baseline fact (S1) that does not depend on any hidden information, yet it passes in every rollout. While the other checks (C2-C7) correctly fail because the lone decision-maker defaults to standard operating procedures (e.g., digital materials, bus delivery, voicemail) instead of the specific changes required by PF1-PF4, the presence of C1 as a passing check for a single agent suggests the benchmark is measuring trivial shared knowledge rather than multi-agent coordination.
